title: CrowdSec Hub conversion and update input (v0.5, D39; v0.6, D73)
description: Input of the crowdsec-hub vectors: one decision of the CrowdSec Hub source (contract/crowdsec, rules in crowdsec-hub.md). Four ops: convert one hub rule, check one downloaded index, which set loads at start, the verdict on a measured set cost. The effect of a rule, the state switch and the scope checks are rule-effect vectors (D73).

state.description: The one switch of the source. off: no rules, no fetch. detect (the default, also in automatic blocking mode): rules run, nothing blocks. block: rules block in gateway mode autoblock, a new or changed rule stays in detect for the settling period.

setCost.description: D43: the verdict on one measured sample (crowdsec.CheckSetCost, section 6). The timing itself is the gateway's and not in the vectors.

baseline_ns.description: Nanoseconds per probe request without hub rules.

reference_ns.description: With the image snapshot; equal to the baseline without a snapshot.

rounds.description: Finished rounds of the probe set.

name.description: Hub item name as in the index. Not constrained here: a bad name is a refusal of the rule (bad_name), not a broken input.

content.description: The decoded YAML of the rule, as text.

description.description: Description of the index, used when the YAML has none.

index.description: The bytes of .index.json as text. Never validated by a schema: a broken index is a refusal with a code, not a broken input.

previous.description: The running set: what it knows about each rule. Absent: no set is running.

limits.description: Lower bounds for vectors only, so that they stay small. The gateway uses the defaults of crowdsec-hub.md section 6.

shrink_base.description: D43: the rule count a new set is held against: the image snapshot. Absent or 0: no snapshot, the running set counts. -1: no check, a pin.

valid.description: Parses, digests match, at least one rule loads and it compiles.

time.description: The date of the set (crowdsec.Set.Time). Not constrained here: absent, unreadable or too far in the future means no date, a rule of its own.
